title: Gaussian density integral bound
statement: Let $v$ be a nonzero nonnegative real number, let $c\in\mathbb R$, and let $g,b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$. Suppose $b$ is integrable with respect to the Gaussian measure of mean $c$ and variance $v$, and $|g(z)|\le b(z)$ for every $z$. Then \[\left|\int_{\mathbb R}p_{c,v}(z)g(z)\,dz\right|\le\int_{\mathbb R}b(z)\,dN(c,v)(z),\] where $p_{c,v}$ is the Gaussian density and $N(c,v)$ is that Gaussian measure.
hypotheses_covered: $v$ is a nonzero nonnegative real number
$b$ is integrable with respect to the Gaussian measure of mean $c$ and variance $v$
replaced: Let $v>0$ and $p_v(c,z)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-c)^2/(2v))$. Let $c\in\mathbb R$ and $g,b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$. If $b$ is integrable for $N(c,v)$ and $|g(z)|\le b(z)$ for every $z$, then $|\int p_v(c,z)g(z)\,dz|\le\int b(z)\,dN(c,v)(z)$, with a nonintegrable integral on the left assigned value zero.
